So the CLI already emits, unconditionally and with no flag, the output shape the mode is designed to produce. There is no 'visual terminal interface' here to replace. OK (time)` with failures to stderr :1992, and the summary :2006/:2008 `OK 3/3 passed in 1.2s`. Every line is newline-terminated and prefixed with an explicit `[i/N]` step label. The spinner is the single thing standing between this command and that output, and --no-spinner removes it. (3d) 'NONE OF THE THREE EXISTS' ALSO OVERSTATES. correctedState: The three Claude identifiers are absent (grep -ra for axScreenReader / AX_SCREEN_READER: 0 product hits), but the divergence they are meant to evidence is not. Claude's screen reader mode replaces a full-screen Ink conversation TUI; this fork has none to replace. Its conversational, permission-approving surface is the Electron GUI, which a screen reader reads through the DOM accessibility tree natively - 286 ARIA/role attributes across apps/electron/src/renderer and packages/ui/src, including role="status"/role="alert" live regions, aria-modal dialogs and aria-activedescendant listboxes. Its CLI (nessy-general-agent, a thin RPC client) is already plain linear labelled text: zero box-drawing characters, no ink/blessed/ora/boxen dependency, and the only in-place redraw sequences in the whole apps/cli/src tree are the two inside createSpinner (index.ts:277, :284). That spinner has a single call site, :1905-1906 in runValidation, so it is confined to the validate command's step progress and never touches the streaming conversation path (:470-539), which appends text_delta and prints labelled '[tool: <name>]' lines unconditionally. The claim that --no-spinner 'does not switch to labelled linear output' is the reverse of the code: with the spinner off, runValidation prints only newline-terminated, [i/N]-labelled lines (:1914, :1921, :1923, :1959, :1981, :1992, :2006). Suppression is reachable per-session by flag (--no-spinner / --disable-spinner), per-shell by NO_COLOR, and automatically when piped (gate at :1905 with _useColor at :254). Residual, much narrower than filed: there is no persistent settings-file key for it, and the flag is named after the spinner rather than after the accessibility need, so it is not discoverable as one. That is a naming and discoverability wish on one command's progress display, not a missing screen-reader mode.
